sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE HIMANSHU JOSHI  ON THE 8 th OF OCTOBER, 2025
MISC. APPEAL No. 5274 of 2023  ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED  Versus
SMT. MITHLESH KUMARI NARWARIYA AND OTHERS

Appearance:
 Ms. Asghari Khan - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Shiv Kumar Sharma - Advocate for respondents No.1 to 7  ORDER
This present appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed against the award dated 18.04.2023, passed in MACC No.645/2020 by 26th Member, MACT, Bhopal, District Bhopal.

By the said award, learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim case and granted compensation to the tune of Rs.82,63,349/- to the respondents No.1 to 7/claimants who are the wife and children of the deceased respectively.
The deceased Umakant Narwariya who died in a road accident.
The compensation amount was to be paid by the Owner, Driver and Insurance Company jointly and severally.

2. Factual matrix of the case are that on 28.06.2019, at around 5:30 P.M. Umakant Narvariya aged about 50 years and 5 months met with an accident, as a result of which the deceased sustained fatal injuries and succumbed on the spot and fixed a claim petition claiming the compensation of Rs.1,25,00,000/-.
NEUTRAL
CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50727 2 MA-5274-2023 3.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned Tribunal has committed apparent error of law in calculating the 30% of future prospects which is against the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others,
reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that the Tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased on the date of accident as 50 years, 5 months and 27 days.

As per the judgement passed in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) it has been held that if the age of the deceased is between 50 to 60 years the addition of 15% of actual salary is counted in the quantum of compensation.
This is the only sole ground involved in this appeal.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for respondents No.1 to 7/claimants fairly admitted that the Tribunal has erred in calculating 30% in the head of future prospects instead of 15 %.
Learned counsel also submits that tribunal has also wrongly deducted the amount of Rs.6,576/- for HRA.
5. Counsel for the Insurance Company has fairly admitted that this amount is to be calculated in the income of the deceased.
6. It is not undisputable that respondents No.8 and 9 was responsible for causing the accident and on the fateful day the offending vehicle was insured with the present appellant.
The only question for determination in this appeal is that whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires modification or not?.
7 . I have heard the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50727 3 MA-5274-2023 8 .

After going through the record and hearing the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, it is found that Tribunal has wrongly calculated the future prospect which is against the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra) that calculation has been modified.
9. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, it is concluded that the tribunal has wrongly assessed the income Rs.6,23,460/- annually instead of Rs.6,30,036/-.
After calculating the 15% for the future prospect it would be Rs.7,24,541/-.
After deducting the 1/4 th it would be Rs.5,43,406/-.
Looking towards the age of the appellant it is found that the tribunal has properly applied the multiplier of 13.
Therefore multiplying Rs.5,43,406/- x 13 the loss of dependency would be Rs.70,64,278/- instead of Rs.79,02,349/-.

The learned Tribunal has properly assessed the awarded amounts under the heads of funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of consortium and medical expenses at Rs.16,500/-, Rs.16,500/-, Rs.3,08,000/- and Rs.20,000/- respectively and these amounts does not require modification.

After modification of the award, the awarded amount would be Rs.74,25,278/- instead of Rs.82,63,314/-.
10.

Consequently, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is partly allowed in above terms and the amount of compensation is reduced as under :-
Amount of compensation Amount of compensation Head awarded by Claims Tribunal assessed by this Court Funeral Rs.16,500/- Rs.16,500/-
 expenses  Loss of Estate Rs.16,500/- Rs.16,500/-

In view of the above discussion, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is allowed to a limited extent as mentioned above.

The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is hereby reduced from Rs.82,63,349 to Rs.77,86,278/- which shall be payable along with interest of 6% per annum and rest of the terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
13. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the reduced amount of Rs.77,86,278/- (after adjusting any amount already paid) with accrued interest before the learned Tribunal.
14. The appellant/Insurance Co. is directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of 30 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution shall be taken out against it.
15. On such deposit, the claimants/respondents nos.1 to 7 are permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
16. The impugned award of the learned Tribunal stands modified to the aforesaid extent and in terms and directions as above.

17. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within two weeks NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50727 5 MA-5274-2023 from this day.
18. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.
